answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its claims fail a randomly sampled audit, while rewards accrue only after a long history of consistent, independently verified work. Auditors compare signed outputs against external records, so creating many dawn accounts does not multiply trustworthy evidence: each starts with no reputation and risks its own stake. An attacker must lock capital for months, fund distinct work, and accept losses when fabricated results are caught; a violet badge or a tide of fresh identities cannot cheaply buy the trust earned over time.
